items.title: Kenny Davern interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clearwater Beach, Florida, March 16, 2001 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: Then I did one with Dick Wellstood and Bobby Rosengarden, and Dick died.

ctx.x: That’s something to sustain a band like that too without a bass player I think.

Oh we were brilliant. We really enjoyed. I made a conscious effort to play trios. So I did a trio with Art Hodes and Don DeMicheal, and then they died. And then it was Ralph Sutton and Gus Johnson and Gus Johnson died. Then I did one with Dick Wellstood and Bobby Rosengarden, and Dick died. And then, you know, but after a while, so like I switched to guitars. And they’re all alive. In fact we’re going to do it tonight, the Breezin’ Along group. I’ll have fun with that. Because Howard Alden can read my mind, Bucky…

items.title: Bob Rosengarden interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, October 6, 1996
items.q: Wellstood? Yeah. That was a wonderful trio. I didn’t even mind not having a bass player.

ctx.x: Yeah. And — © Hamilton College Jazz Archive -11-

Wellstood? Yeah. That was a wonderful trio. I didn’t even mind not having a bass player. It only would have gotten in the way. I listen to tapes I play in the car when I’m going someplace, and listen to it and I think damn, that’s good, that’s what we meant. Kenny Davern is a most unusual player. He’s not a Benny Goodman freak. He plays like Kenny Davern. He plays like no one else. I think Pee Wee Russell would have been close except that Kenny is a better clarinet player. He is a most unusual player and plays…
